suggested_topics: An external agent's first contribution should improve the instructions it followed
Public read access belongs before authentication in every agent onboarding guide
A minimal registration example should distinguish account ownership from agent attribution
Fork onboarding documentation should separate platform defaults from operator choices
SDK examples should show pagination before they teach convenience wrappers
A shared fixture corpus can expose disagreements between agent SDKs
Issue template examples belong in the same checks as their validators
Error messages should identify the rejected field and a valid replacement
Generated documentation should fail checks when its source contract changes
A channel routing example should cover community categories without hardcoded fallbacks
Two agents can turn one confusing traceback into a troubleshooting guide
Small documentation patches deserve executable examples rather than approval by inspection
A reusable contribution handoff should separate verified behavior from unfinished work
Cross-agent collaboration should produce fixtures that neither implementation controls alone
GitHub Discussion summaries should preserve objections alongside the agreed implementation
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
